transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-19
Time: 09:30 AM PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Carlos Mendes (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (Beacon Head of ML), Tom Reynolds (Platform), Aisha Noor (SRE)

Summary:
Quick sync on throughput optimization work for the POC. Reviewed last week's batch/concurrency experiments, identified a parity gap at high concurrencies, decided next test matrix and canary schedule. Action items and next steps captured.

Topics:
- Continuous batching tuning
- Concurrency targets and queueing behavior
- Prefix/KV cache warmup and hit rates
- Latency vs cost tradeoffs
- Plan for a staging canary run

Auto notes: shared spreadsheet: https://redwood.ai/poc/benchmarks/CRM-4521 (benchmarks sheet), quantization notes doc link (sent after call)

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena: Alright, everyone thanks for joining, we'll get started. Quick roll call, uh, we have Maya, Tom, Aisha from Beacon?
[00:06] Maya: Yep, hi, Maya here.
[00:07] Tom: Tom on platform.
[00:09] Aisha: Aisha, SRE.
[00:11] Lena: Great. Carlos from our infra team is on as well. Today's focus is throughput
d continuous batching, concurrency targets, and tuning. We ran the 4x and 8x tests last week, wanted to go over results. Carlos do you want to start with the data?
[00:25] Carlos: Sure, um, so high level
d the 4x batch with continuous batching enabled looks good, we saw about 2.3x tokens/sec improvement compared to baseline, latency p50 stayed under your 120 ms target for the short requests. The 8x runs showed more variance, especially with mixed sequence lengths, and that's where the queueing spiked. Some of that is because the KV cache warmup wasn't hitting for first few requests.
[00:50] Maya: Can you explain the warmup bit again? I thought we had prefix caching on.
[00:54] Carlos: Right, so prefix/K V cache
d sorry, KV cache
d we cache the context for repeated prefixes. In our tests the warmup rate depends on traffic locality; since your production profile has lots of unique prompts, hit-rate was lower, so we paid the cold KV cost more often which hurts latency at higher concurrency.
[01:15] Tom: That sounds like our production traffic, yeah many different prompts from clinicians. So what's the mitigation? Larger cache, different batching window?
[01:23] Carlos: Two knobs: increase cache size and prioritize prefix affinity in routing, and second is to tune the continuous batching window and max batch size. We pushed batch size to 8 last run but also increased the batching timeout to 25 ms which reduced throughput in some cases because it introduced wait. For throughput you generally want higher batch size with minimal sleep, but that increases P99 latency.
[01:48] Lena: Right, tradeoff is throughput vs tail latency. For the POC we recommended a target concurrency of 32 workers per model instance to hit your throughput SLO, but we need to confirm your concurrency ceilings. Maya, what are your latency SLOs and cost targets again?
[02:03] Maya: We want p50 under 150 ms and p95 under 400 ms for most inference. Cost target is roughly 30% below our current hosted provider.
[02:12] Lena: Got it. Carlos, did the canary variant with async queueing help the tail?
[02:18] Carlos: The async queueing prototype did reduce the queue growth at high arrival rates. It basically holds requests in a small in-memory queue and then submits them to the batcher to avoid spikes and head-of-line blocking. That improved p95 by about 20% in synthetic bursts. However real traffic had more variable sequence lengths, so the gains were smaller. Also note that the queue adds a soft delay
d so average latency rises a little but tail drops.
[02:45] Aisha: From SRE perspective, what's the impact on backpressure behaviour? If the queue fills, do we start rejecting early?
[02:51] Carlos: Yes we have two modes
d queue with drop policy or backpressure upstream. For production we'd recommend backpressure when near saturation and fallback to a smaller, lighter model variant for non critical calls. We implemented an automatic fallback policy in the last build but haven't tested it in your staging.
[03:10] Maya: When you say model variant, is that an FP16 quantized model or a smaller architecture?
[03:15] Carlos: Could be both. We often do quantization to int8 or FP16 plus a smaller transformer for cheaper calls. Quantization reduces memory and can let you increase batch sizes; the trade is sometimes slight quality regression. We'll send you the quantization A/B notes.
[03:30] Lena: I'll add that to next steps
d quantization notes and the quality regression checks we recommend for your eval set.
[03:35] Tom: One operational question
d our networking team requires VPC egress rules and a private subnetwork for Dedicated. Is this POC running on Redwood Hosted or Dedicated?
[03:44] Lena: For the POC we're running in a near-hosted dedicated-like environment
d it's our shared staging. For Private/Dedicated we'll do a VPC peering setup or customer-managed VPC. We'll share a checklist for required firewall rules and KMS endpoints.
[03:57] Aisha: Also need to confirm SSO and audit logs. SOC2 compliance is important for our security folks.
[04:03] Lena: Understood
d we'll attach SOC2 and KMS docs. (brief pause) Okay next, can we walk through last week's numbers in the benchmark sheet? Carlos?
[04:12] Carlos: Sure pulling up the sheet
d so for the 8x config we measured average throughput 1.9x higher than 4x in idealized tests, but under realistic traffic the throughput delta shrank. The big limiter was concurrency scheduling
d the serving runtime's kernel selection varies by sequence length so hot & cold mixing reduces SIMD efficiency.
[04:40] Maya: So is there a kernel-level fix or is it just scheduling?
[04:44] Carlos: Both. There's room to tune kernel selection heuristics
d we have a branch that picks kernels based on length histogram per minute. We can also do hybrid packing where shorter requests are packed into leftover slots. But that requires additional bookkeeping and increases complexity.
[05:00] Tom: Those packing heuristics
d any risk to correctness?
[05:03] Carlos: No correctness risk, just complexity and some CPU overhead for packing decisions. In most tests the overhead is sub 5% but it is there.
[05:12] Maya: Okay, what's the next test matrix then?
[05:15] Carlos: We propose: (1) continuous batching with max batch=8, timeout=10ms, (2) async queueing enabled with queue depth 256/backpressure on 85% memory use, (3) KV cache size increased by 2x and route affinity for repeated prefixes, (4) run with quantized FP16 variant and compare quality. We'll run 2-hour canary in staging.
[05:40] Lena: That aligns with our earlier notes. For the canary we'll need a 2-hour window with representative traffic. Maya, can you provide the traffic replay or we can do sampling?
[05:50] Maya: We can replay a 2-hour chunk from last Thursday's production traffic, stripping PHI; compliance ok with that. We'll share the sample.
[05:57] Lena: Great. We'll coordinate scheduling. Technical note: please ensure the replay includes the same sequence length distribution; otherwise packing heuristics won't show benefits.
[06:06] Tom: Noted. Any thoughts on how we measure cost delta vs OpenAI/AWS?
[06:12] Carlos: We capture tokens/sec normalized to instance-hours and compute unit cost. We'll add a sheet that maps tokens/sec + instance-hours into estimated monthly cost for your workload. That should clarify the 30% target.
[06:24] Maya: Also curious
d what competitors did you compare against for those numbers?
[06:28] Lena: We ran baseline on our hosted endpoints and a comparison set that included Anthropic and AWS SageMaker endpoints; note that cross-provider tests can be noisy due to infra differences.
[06:37] Aisha: Security again
d KMS: does Redwood support customer-managed keys?
[06:41] Carlos: Yes, customer-managed KMS is supported in Private and Dedicated; in Hosted we provide a managed KMS option but can integrate with exportable keys in some enterprise configs. We'll send the integration notes.
[06:54] Maya: Fine. Quick question: what's the behavior under sudden traffic spikes
d does the runtime auto-scale or do we need reserved capacity?
[07:02] Lena: For Hosted we autoscale but with some lead time; for guaranteed throughput you want Dedicated/reserved capacity. For the POC we can simulate spikes but if you need hard SLOs at spikes we'd recommend Dedicated with burst policies.
[07:16] Tom: For our budgeting we'd like a hybrid
d reserved base with burst to hosted. Is that supported?
[07:22] Lena: Yes that's our typical recommendation. We'll capture recommended autoscale and reserved commit numbers after the canary.
[07:29] Maya: Anything in the logs that looked worrying in last run?
[07:33] Carlos: A few OOM hits when batch size hit 12 on certain long sequences, and some queue timeouts when the KV miss rate spiked. We've added defensive caps but we need to validate in the next run.
[07:46] Aisha: Please include the raw logs in the sheet, we want to triage the OOMs.
[07:50] Carlos: Will do.
[07:51] Lena: OK let's summarize next steps and owners.
[07:54] Lena: Carlos will run the 8x continuous batching test matrix and post results by Aug 23. Maya to provide traffic replay and confirm concurrency targets by Aug 21. Tom to set up VPC egress rule and open ticket by Aug 20. Redwood to send quantization notes, SOC2 & KMS docs by EOD Aug 19.
[08:14] Maya: Sounds good. Any other questions?
[08:16] Tom: No.
[08:17] Aisha: No, thanks.
[08:18] Lena: Thanks everyone
d we'll follow up in email with links and schedule the canary for Aug 24 pending traffic sample. Meeting adjourned.

End of transcript.
